questions.q: Charge is distributed within a sphere of radius $R$ with a volume charge density $ρ\left(r\right) = \dfrac{A}{r^{2}}e^{- \dfrac{2r}{a}},$ where $A$ and $a$ are constants. If $Q$ is the total charge of this charge distribution, the radius $R$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$ρ\left(r\right) = \dfrac{A}{r^{2}}e^{- \dfrac{2r}{a}}$



Charge enclosed between $r$ and $r + dr$ is

$dq = ρ\left(r\right)4\pir^{2}dr$

To get total charge $Q^{}$

$Q = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{R}dq = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{R}\dfrac{A}{r2}e^{- 2r / a}4\pir^{2}dr= - 4\pi A\dfrac{a}{2}{[ e^{- 2r / a} ]}_{0}^{R}$

$Q = - 4\piA\dfrac{a}{2} \left[e^{- 2R / a} - 1\right]$

$R = - \ln \left[1 - $\dfrac{Q2}{4\pi Aa}\right]\dfrac{a}{2} = \dfrac{a}{2}$\ln \left(\dfrac{1}{1 - \dfrac{Q}{2\pi aA}}\right)

$

questions.q: The electrostatic potential due to an electric dipole at a distance $r$ varies as :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The potential at a distance $r$ due to a short dipole is ${V}_{dip}\left(r\right) = \dfrac{1}{4\pi{ε}_{∘}}\dfrac{\overset{\to}{p} \cdot \overset{^}{r}}{r^{2}}$, where $\overset{\to}{p}$=dipole moment.

questions.q: A positive charge particle of $100$ mg is thrown in opposite direction to a uniform electric field of strength $1 \times {10}^{5}NC^{- 1}$. If the charge on the particle is $40\muC$ and the initial velocity is $200\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$, how much distance it will travel before coming to the rest momentarily
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Force experienced by a particle with charge $q$~in an electric field~$F = qE$.

Now,~the acceleration produced is given as~$a = \dfrac{F}{m} = \dfrac{qE}{m}= \dfrac{40 \times {10}^{- 6} \times {10}^{5}}{1 \times {10}^{- 4}}$

$= 4 \times {10}^{4}ms^{- 2}$~ (As the particle is projected against the electric field, hence it is~decelerated)

Using,~$v^{2} = u^{2} - 2as$

We have,~${0}^{2} = u^{2} - 2as$

$s = \dfrac{v2}{2a} = \dfrac{\left(200\right)2}{2 \times 4 \times {10}^{4}} = 0 . 5m$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As electric field is uniform, so force acting on the charged particle will be uniform.

Therefore,

${W}_{E} = \overset{→}{F} \cdot \overset{→}{s} = q\overset{→}{E} \cdot \overset{→}{s}$

$= \left(2 \times {10}^{- 2}\right)\left[30\overset{^}{i} \cdot \left[\left(0\overset{^}{i} + 0\overset{^}{j} + 0\overset{^}{k}\right) - \left(\overset{^}{i} +2\overset{^}{j} + 0\overset{^}{k}\right)\right]\right]$

$= - 60 \times {10}^{- 2}J$

$= - 600mJ

$

questions.q: Two isolated metallic solid spheres of radii $R$ and $2R$ are charged such that both have same charge density $\sigma$ . The spheres are then connected by a thin conducting wire. If the new charge density of the bigger sphere is ${σ}^{'}$. The ratio $\dfrac{\sigma '}{σ}$& is :

Charge and charge density on both isolated metallic solid spheres are show below.

Let the charges and the charge densities on both the spheres after connected by thin conducting wire& be& ${Q}_{1}^{'}, {Q}_{2}^{'}, \sigma\text{and}{σ}^{'}$~as shown below.

Once connected,~charge on both the spheres will redistribute such that~potentials at the surface of both spheres is the same.

$∴ \dfrac{k{Q}_{1}^{'}}{R} = \dfrac{k{Q}_{2}^{'}}{2R}$

$⇒ {Q}_{1}^{'}4{πε}_{0}R = \dfrac{{Q}_{2}^{'}}{4\pi{ε}_{0}\left(2R\right)}$

Using charge conservation,~

${Q}_{1}^{'} + {Q}_{2}^{'} = {Q}_{1} + {Q}_{2}$

$\dfrac{3}{2}{Q}_{2}^{'} = 20{πR}^{2}\sigma$

$∴ \dfrac{\sigma '}{σ} = \dfrac{5}{6}$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason(R)
Assertion (A) : Work done by electric field on moving a positive charge on an equipotential surface is always zero.
Reason (R) : Electric lines of forces are always perpendicular to equipotential surfaces.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The equipotential surfaces are surfaces where the electric potential is the same at every point. In other words, there is no potential difference along an equipotential surface. Since work done $( W )$ is given by the equation $W = q ∆ V$, and there is no potential difference on an equipotential surface, the work done is always zero.

As there is no force along the surface of the equipotential surface, the electric field must be perpendicular to the surface.

Hence, while both statements are correct, the reason (R) is providing the correct explanation for why the work done on a positive charge on an equipotential surface is always zero.

Experimentally it is found that $12 . 8eV$ energy is required to separate a hydrogen atom into a proton and an electron. So the orbital radius of the electron in a hydrogen atom is~$\dfrac{9}{x} \times {10}^{- 10}m$.

The value of the $x$ is: _____.

($1eV = 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19}J, \dfrac{1}{4\pi{ε}_{0}} = 9 \times {10}^{9}\dfrac{Nm2}{C2}$~and electronic charge~$= 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19}C$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The given data is&

$q = 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19}C\dfrac{1}{4{πε}_{0}} = 9 \times {10}^{9}Nm^{2}C^{- 2}$

The formula for the value of energy in a hydrogen atom is given by~

$E = \dfrac{q2}{8\pi{ε}_{0}r} ⇒ E = \dfrac{q2}{2 ( 4\pi{ε}_{0} ) r}$

$⇒ r = \dfrac{9 \times {10}^{9} \times 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19}}{12 . 8 \times 2}$

$⇒ r = \dfrac{9}{16} \times {10}^{- 10}m$

It is given that~$r = \dfrac{9}{x} \times {10}^{- 10}m ⇒ \dfrac{9}{16} \times {10}^{- 10} = \dfrac{9}{x} \times {10}^{- 10} ⇒ x = 16$
